question: You glance at a trusted clock that, unknown to you, stopped exactly twelve hours ago. Do you know the time?
answer: No, though your belief is true and well grounded. Bertrand Russell used the stopped clock in 1948; Edmund Gettier's three-page paper of 1963 made the point famous: truth plus good reasons can still be luck. Philosophers have spent sixty years hunting for the missing ingredient that turns a lucky hit into knowledge.
move: Being right and having good reasons can still add up to luck.
ask: Which of my recent good calls was skill, and which just happened to come out right?
reference: Gettier, Is Justified True Belief Knowledge?, Analysis 23 (6), 1963; Russell, Human Knowledge: Its Scope and Limits, Allen & Unwin, 1948
